tools.name: list_tables
tools.description: List every table in one database with its row count. Use it to find the table that answers a question before calling describe_table.

tools.name: describe_table
tools.description: Return the fields (name, type, description), the table description and the row count of one table. Always call this before writing SQL: many source columns are stored as text and need try_cast.

tools.name: query
tools.description: Run one read-only SQL statement (SELECT, WITH, SHOW or DESCRIBE) in the Amazon Athena (Trino) dialect and return up to 1,000 rows with column names and bytes scanned. findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "list_tables" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: List every table in one database with its row count. Use it to find the table that answers a question before calling describe_table.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "query" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.
